action: Autopay advises its customers to check their transaction history and report unrecognised transactions to their bank promptly, and warns about messages and calls citing the cyberattack.
date_note: Date Autopay says it detected the unauthorized access; reported 14-15 November
exec: A Polish payment operator's breach may include card data; some banks reportedly blocked cards, and the number affected is not stated.
plain: Polish payment company Autopay says someone got into part of its systems and some payment data, possibly including card details. At least two banks blocked some cards, a report says; no number of people is given.
summary: Autopay S.A. says it detected unauthorized access on 11 November to part of its infrastructure and payment data, which may include email addresses, top-up phone numbers, IP addresses and card data used for transactions, not banking logins. It notified UODO, police and CSIRT KNF; its spokesperson says processing was unaffected. Autopay told Sekurak the attack was most likely LLM-assisted. Citing Niebezpiecznik, money.pl reports at least two banks blocked some cards.
title: Autopay (Poland) reports unauthorized access to payment data, says attack used AI tools

validation.note: money.pl, Spider's Web and android.com.pl relay Autopay's own statement; the bank card blocking rests on Niebezpiecznik as relayed by money.pl (19 Nov), which does not name the banks. No independent confirmation of scope.

review.note: stronger than the source / missing statement: title says Autopay says AI tools were used but summary omitted it; summary now attributes the LLM-assisted statement to Autopay (told Sekurak, relayed by Spider's Web and android.com.pl), the processing-unaffected statement to its spokesperson, bank card
